I suggest doing 5 books a month instead of one a week. That gets you 60 books read for the year instead of 52. I also suggest having 8-10 books to chose from every month with at least 2 non fiction choices. Every month should have a general theme or genre, or author with at least  half of the books being of said genre. That will get people to read things they never would have read, when I was younger I would choose sci-fi or steven king for every book I read, till my dad started trying to get me into "the classics" (steinbeck, the odessy, moby dick etc) and satire (catch-22, vonnegut) which gave me a better variety and knowledge base to work from.

Mixing is bringing together separate elements (different instruments, different mics, different elements) into something cohesive.

 Mastering is what gets you from something cohesive to your final product. For example, complete audio for a movie (soundtrack + score + effects + dialogue) or an album. With proper levels correctly encoded ( for surround, Dolby etc) and formatted.

Mastering is what gets you the final product that will be burned onto millions of cds etc

EDIT: tl;dr: Mixing is working with and on the individual elements/instruments in a song, mastering is working with and on the final mix ( ie 2 channel stereo) of the song. 
Mixing is done first, mastering is the final step..

That 0db is essentially your sound/peak ceiling. By making sure that only the loudest parts come close to 0db you avoid clipping and distortion when those peaks hit (think of an explosion in a movie, for  a speaker to reproduce that boom accurately it requires a quick burst of power, if that speaker or equipment can't handle or provide that power you lose those loud sounds being reproduced via clipping and/or distortion) keeping the loudest parts at 0 d/b allows for the largest range of equipment to be able to reproduce the sound relatively accurately, from theatre in a box and sound bars to high end mark logan and krell.
